claims.verbatim: The French physician Armond Trous- seau (1801-1867) stated,” when an indi- vidual in good health takes sub-nitrate of bismuth, the only phenomenon to be no- ticed is constipation, but the nervous func- tions, the animal heat, the movements of the heart, the urinary and cutaneous secre- tions are not influenced in an appreciable manner.” In 1868 Adolf Kussmaul used bismuth to treat gastric ulcers. Bismuth is still in general use today as an OTC (over the counter “drug”) to soothe the irritated gas- trointestinal tract, diarrhea and dispepsia as the tasty pink Pepto Bismol!!
claims.claim_text: Wallach relays that taking bismuth, the active ingredient still sold today as Pepto-Bismol, reliably produces constipation.
auditor_flags: quote-attributed: Armond Trousseau, reproduced by Wallach

claims.verbatim: Before long this magnesium rich spring was found to produce water that was beneficial for external and internal medical use. For the next 10 years only the local people used this healing spring; about that time Lord Dudley North “under a melan- choly disposition (constipation, depres- sion), drank the mineral waters as a medi- cine and noted it to be a very effective pur- gative.” “Epsom Water” was rapidly ac- cepted as an internal remedy and purifier of the blood.
claims.claim_text: Wallach recounts that magnesium-rich Epsom water was taken as a medicine for constipation and prized as a very effective purgative.
auditor_flags: quote-attributed: Lord Dudley North, historical account reproduced by Wallach

claims.verbatim: Maybrick became seriously ill in April 26, 1889 and his doctor was summoned because of headaches (hypoglycemia or diabetes resulting from chromium and va- nadium deficiencies), numbness ( B,, defi- ciency) of his legs and leg cramps (calcium deficiency) so bad “they were like iron bars.”
claims.claim_text: In the Maybrick case Wallach reads leg cramps so severe "they were like iron bars" as a calcium deficiency, and the accompanying leg numbness as a B-vitamin deficiency — a vivid picture of mineral-starved legs.

claims.verbatim: A. Six year olds drawing of a giraffe before high sugar breakfast. B. Same six year olds drawing of a giraffe one and a half hours after a high sugar breakfast. Simple method for diagnosing ADD and ADHD associated with high sugar low Cr, V and Li diets.
claims.claim_text: Wallach shows the effect of sugar on behavior with a child's own drawings — a six-year-old's giraffe drawn before a high-sugar breakfast versus the same child's degraded drawing an hour and a half after — as a simple at-home way to spot sugar-driven ADD/ADHD tied to low chromium, vanadium and lithium.

claims.verbatim: Table 7-8. Common Degenerative Diseases of Humans and Their Cause. Osteoporosis: Ca, Mg, B, Cu, S Arthritis (Ankylosing spondylitis): Ca, Mg, B, Cu, S Hypertension: Ca, Mg, B Bone spurs, heel spurs, Ca deposits: Ca, Mg, B
claims.claim_text: Wallach attributes osteoporosis and ankylosing spondylitis, an inflammatory low-back arthritis, to deficiencies of calcium, magnesium, boron, copper and sulfur.

claims.verbatim: Muscle Relaxants, Spasm Relievers — Mineral Replacement: Ca, Mg, B, Li: Cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril) - Causes dizziness, drowsiness, fainting, falls. Orphenidrine (Norflex, Norgesic) - Causes dizziness, drowsiness, fainting, falls. Methocarbamol (Roboxin) - Causes dizziness, drowsiness, falls.
claims.claim_text: Wallach flags common muscle relaxants - cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril), orphenadrine (Norflex), and methocarbamol (Robaxin) - as causing dizziness, drowsiness and falls, and offers calcium, magnesium, boron and lithium as the mineral replacement.

claims.verbatim: Calcarea Fluor (Fluoride of lime) - is found in the surface of the bones, in the enamel of the teeth and in the elastic tibers of the skin, muscular tissue and blood vessels. A deficiency results in a relaxed condition of the tissues and is a predisposing cause in a number of diseases. It is indicated in ailments which can be traced to a relaxed condition of elastic fibers, including dilation of the blood vessels, haemorrhoids, enlarged varicose veins, hardened glands, cracks in the skin, etc.
claims.claim_text: Rare Earths reprints Schuessler's cell-salt table, which lists Calcarea Fluor (calcium fluoride) — a component of the elastic fibers of skin and blood vessels — for the relaxed elastic fibers behind dilated vessels, hemorrhoids, and enlarged varicose veins.
auditor_flags: source: Schuessler 12 Cell Salts table reprinted in the book (Table 11-1), not Wallach's own protocol

claims.verbatim: Calcarea Sulph (Sulphate of Lime) - is found in the epithelial cells in the blood. It acts as a preventitive of cell disintegration and ‘suppuration. A deficiency allows suppuration to continue too long; therefore, wounds that are too slow to heal (i.e.- catarrhs, boils, carbuncles, ulcers, abscesses, pimples and pustules of the face) need this remedy.
claims.claim_text: In Wallach's rundown of Schuessler's cell salts, Calcarea Sulph (sulphate of lime) is named as the remedy for slow-healing skin eruptions, including pimples and pustules of the face.
auditor_flags: homeopathic Schuessler cell-salt (tissue-salt) system as reproduced in Rare Earths; 'pimples and pustules of the face' maps to acne

claims.verbatim: If all of the mineral levels in the hair analysis are universally low it indicates maldigestion ( hypochlorhydria - low stomach acid) and/or malabsorption ( celiac disease - wheat gluten or cows milk albumen allergy).
claims.claim_text: Wallach says a hair analysis showing all minerals uniformly low points to malabsorption -- often from a hidden wheat gluten or cow's milk allergy damaging the gut.

claims.verbatim: SYMPTOMS of HYPOTHYROIDISM (Hashimoto's Disease) Fatigue Cold intolerance Muscle aches & pains Heavy or more frequent periods Low sex drive Brittle nails Weight gain Hair loss Muscle cramps Depression Constipation
claims.claim_text: Wallach lists muscle aches, pains, and cramps among the symptoms of hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's disease), so a sluggish thyroid can be part of why the legs cramp and ache.

claims.verbatim: Vegetarians and vegans who do not supplement with minerals rarely have P deficiency, however, because of their high phytic acid intake they always have other mineral deficiencies including Ca, Cu, Cr, V. Li and Zn.
claims.claim_text: Wallach warns that vegetarians and vegans who don't supplement always develop mineral deficiencies -- including bone-building calcium and copper -- because of their high phytic-acid intake.

claims.verbatim: Although the Eskimo diet is comprised 90% of meat (i.e.- whale meat, whale blubber, walrus meat, walrus blubber, reindeer meat, fish, etc.) and bone, they do not have heart disease, cholesterol problems or strokes. The salmon and other cold water fish in their diet provide rich sources of the essential fatty acids required by the liver to properly process cholesterol] and prevent platelet clumping.
claims.claim_text: Wallach points out that traditional Eskimos eat a diet that is roughly 90% meat, blubber and fish yet have no cholesterol problems, because the essential fatty acids in cold-water fish let the liver process cholesterol properly.
